extracted.intended_audience: Experts/peer reviewers and panel members evaluating ERC Synergy Grant proposals (Horizon Europe)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria for individual reviewers, remote referees and panel members assessing ERC Synergy Grant proposals across Steps 1–3, including scoring, required content, reviewer conduct, conflict of interest, confidentiality and data protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence as sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation and is at the core of the peer review evaluation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to both the ground-breaking nature and ambition of the Research Project, and to the intellectual capacity and creativity of the Principal Investigators, focusing on whether the PIs have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project. No other criteria than the evaluation elements defined in the ERC Work Programme must be considered. Incorrect application of the evaluation criterion or application of irrelevant criteria is a procedural error that may justify re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — ground-breaking nature and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the Research Project focusing on ground-breaking nature and potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation questions (Annex 1): To what extent does the proposed research address important scientific questions? To what extent are the project's objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art and will advance the frontier of knowledge? To what extent does the proposal go beyond what the individual Principal Investigators could achieve alone? (Step 2 additions) To what extent are the research methodology and working arrangements appropriate to achieve the goals of the project? To what extent are the timescales and resources adequate and properly justified? Synergy Grants only: To what extent do the PIs propose a combination of scientific approaches crucial to address the scope and complexity of the research questions?

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigators — intellectual capacity and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the PIs' ability and track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation questions (Annex 1): To what extent have the PIs demonstrated the ability to conduct ground‑breaking research? To what extent do the PIs provide evidence of creative and original thinking? To what extent do the PIs have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project? For Synergy grants: does the group demonstrate the combined know‑how (skills, experience, expertise, disciplines, teams) necessary to address the proposed research question (based on the Extended Synopsis)? Preprints properly referenced with DOI may be taken into consideration in assessing track records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part II content and implementation details requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Part II of the proposal must explain project implementation in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part II should include research methodology, work plan, risk assessment and mitigating measures, justification for the requested budget and resources, and any further necessary background not in Part I. Reviewers at Step 2 evaluate the complete proposal including Part II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal numerical marking scale (Research Project)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical marks awarded for the Research Project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks range from 5 (Outstanding), 4 (Excellent), 3 (Very Good), 2 (Good) to 1 (Non‑competitive), with the possibility of awarding half marks. Provide explanatory comments and ensure marks are consistent with comments. Use of the full range of marks is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigators qualitative assessment scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall qualitative assessment options for the Principal Investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five-option multiple-choice format: Outstanding / Excellent / Very Good / Good / Non‑competitive. Explanatory comments for PIs may optionally be provided at Step 2. Comments should be consistent with the qualitative choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote Referees three-option recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation options for Remote Referees during Step 2 remote evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote Referees award a qualitative three-option recommendation on the proposal: highly recommended, recommended, or not recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag question (Step 1) — retain for Step 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary evaluative question used in Step 1 individual reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Step 1 reviewers (Chairs, Vice Chairs, Members, Evaluators) must answer the 'Flag' question: 'Do you think this proposal should be further evaluated in Step 2?' Panel Chairs and Vice Chairs consider the responses alongside the content of individual reviews when deciding which proposals pass to Step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel scoring categories and outcomes (Step 2 and Step 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of panel scores and funding recommendation outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Step 2 each proposal receives: Score A – sufficient quality to pass to Step 3; Score B – meets some but not all elements of the ERC's excellence criterion. At Step 3 panel scores: Score A – fully meets ERC's excellence criterion and is recommended for funding if sufficient funds available; Score B – meets some but not all elements and will not be funded. Applicants receive Evaluation Reports with final panel score, ranking range, panel comments and individual reviews. Applicants retained for Step 3 (scored A) are not ranked at Step 2; successful Step 3 panels establish final ranking after interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal retention and budgetary cutoff rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule for selecting proposals to be retained for Step 3 based on budgetary cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals will be retained for Step 3 based on the outcome of Step 2 evaluation and a budgetary cutoff level of up to three times the panel's indicative budget. The Synergy Grant call budget is allocated to each panel proportional to the budgetary demand of its assigned proposals to ensure comparable success rates across panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality standards (content, tone and structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for the substance and presentation of individual reviewer comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual reviews must be of good quality, genuine and substantial, and polite. Comments should take the form of a statement and explanation of key strengths and weaknesses of the proposal, and should address the evaluation questions in Annex 1. All individual reviewers' comments are included in the Evaluation Report and reproduced to applicants, so formulate comments carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer language and conduct guidelines (DOs and DON'Ts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed behavioral and drafting guidance for reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO provide substantial, explanatory comments; use dispassionate, analytical and unambiguous language; use grammatically correct, complete, clear sentences with no jargon; ensure critical comments are constructive; make sure comments align with marks/recommendations. DON'T self-declare insufficient expertise (instead inform ERCEA/Chair to reassign), avoid dismissive statements about applicants or their fields, abstain from commenting on age/nationality/gender/personal matters, avoid referencing or comparing with other proposals or previous assessments, avoid copy‑paste from the proposal or other reviews, avoid comments on applicants' Host Institutions, avoid using Journal Impact Factors as a proxy for research quality (use qualitative judgement), be aware of unconscious bias (gender and diversity), note that societal impact is not an ERC evaluation criterion, avoid comments on ethical and security aspects (these are assessed separately after scientific evaluation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources assessment timing and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how reviewers should (or should not) assess resources and budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid recommendations on resources at Step 1 or Step 2 (assessment of resources is done at Step 3). Avoid recommendations on salaries (they depend on national/institutional rules and are eligible costs). If a budget cut is recommended at Step 3, provide proper justification; recommendations for reduction must be documented and explained in panel comments and based on analysis of requested vs necessary resources. Cuts across-the-board are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation expectations prior to panel meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: What reviewers and chairs should do before each panel meeting to ensure efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to meetings reviewers individually and remotely review assigned proposals and recommend Remote Referees for in-depth review. Panel Chairs/Vice Chairs familiarise themselves with proposals and written individual reviews. Prior preparation helps focus discussions on proposals that merit substantial discussion and facilitates early elimination of low-ranked proposals, and helps gather feedback for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: No discussion or disclosure during individual remote review
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction on communication among reviewers during the remote individual review phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the individual remote review evaluation there shall be no discussions of the proposals between reviewers and they should not disclose the proposals assigned for their evaluation to other experts. If a Panel Member considers they have insufficient expertise to evaluate an assigned proposal, they must immediately inform ERCEA's Scientific Officers and the Panel Chair for reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of voting and ranking systems in panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted methods panels may use to reach decisions when consensus is not feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While consensus is preferred, panels may use voting systems (e.g. majority vote with each Panel Member having one vote per proposal) to expedite ranking. Panel Chairs/Members with conflict of interest cannot discuss or vote on the proposal. Panels may also use a cumulative ranking system where Panel Members contribute individual preferred rankings which are summed and averaged to produce a cumulative ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert performance and non‑delegation obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations on how experts perform their contracted work and delegation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts must work independently in a personal capacity (not on behalf of any organisation), perform tasks in a confidential and fair way, to the best of their abilities, professional skills and knowledge, applying the highest ethical standards, and follow instructions and time‑schedule given by the contracting authority. Experts may not delegate the work to other persons nor be replaced by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest (impartiality) rules and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules on situations automatically considered conflicts of interest and their consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts must prevent situations compromising impartiality (family/emotional/political/national affinity, economic interest etc.). Automatic exclusions include being director/trustee/partner/employee/contractor of an entity involved in the proposal (normally excluded from evaluation), involvement in preparation of a proposal in the same call/budget split, benefiting from acceptance/rejection, close family ties with persons involved, membership of advisory groups/work programmes or EU Programme Committees, recent employment/contract/collaboration (within 3 years), scientific rivalry, mentor/mentee relationships, or recent scientific collaboration (Horizon Europe specific). Consequences vary: exclusion from evaluation for the proposal, from competing proposals, or from the entire call. Experts must confirm no conflict for each task and immediately inform contracting authority if conflict arises and stop working until instructions. Breaches may lead to contract termination and other measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on maintaining confidentiality of proposals and evaluation materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the Contract and for five years after last payment experts must keep confidential all 'sensitive information' and may use it only to implement the Contract. They must not disclose confidential information, discuss proposals with others not directly involved (except in meetings with prior approval), disclose details on evaluation process/outcomes, names of other experts, or communicate with applicants/beneficiaries (except when organised by contracting authority). If working on contracting authority premises, experts may not remove documents and must ensure protection of electronic documents; they must return/erase/destroy sensitive information after evaluation if instructed. Confidentiality obligations lapse if contracting authority releases expert, information becomes public by other channels, or disclosure required by law. Breaches may lead to measures set out in the Expert Call for Expression of Interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data protection obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements on processing and protecting personal data during evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts must process personal data only on basis of documented instructions from contracting authority and only for the duration specified in the contract. They must not use personal data for other purposes, must protect personal data with at least the same level of care they use for their own data, not disclose personal data to third parties without written authorisation, promptly address contracting authority queries on data processing, adopt appropriate security measures proportionate to risks, and immediately inform the contracting authority and cooperate in the event of a personal data breach.
